## Why visit

A fresh reason to revisit Liverpool for experienced pub travellers. This March 2026 opening occupies a 1920s banking hall in Pacific Chambers, using its architectural scale for a pub styled after the grand gin palaces. A mezzanine and side rooms offer different perspectives on the space, and the operator advertises a serious rotating cask range rather than relying solely on the building. Its position between the Cavern Quarter and Dale Street makes it a practical additional stop. Compare its new use of a historic commercial interior with the surviving brewery-designed rooms at the Lion or Vines.

## Beer

Operator advertises ten rotating cask ales from local suppliers; CAMRA lists regular and changing cask beers. Actual live range will vary. CAMRA lists Timothy Taylor Landlord and JW Lees Boddingtons Bitter as regulars, with Neptune Abyss stout a recent changing guest.

## Plan the visit

A recent conversion, not an intact Victorian pub. Confirm opening and food service, particularly if making it a meal stop.

**Getting there:** Victoria Street close to Moorfields and the Dale Street walking cluster.
